candidates.title: `Game::Dispose()` raises `Disposed` on every call
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-019 — `Game::Dispose()` raises `Disposed` on every call
**Severity: low · Confidence: VERIFIED · Area: `modules/runtime`**

`Game::Dispose()` calls `Dispose(true)` — which early-returns when already disposed — and then
raises `Disposed` **unconditionally** (`modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp:453-457`). A second
`Dispose()` therefore re-raises the event to every subscriber.
candidates.bible_target_evidence: public `Game::Dispose()` still raises `Disposed` after every idempotent inner call

candidates.title: A throwing component leaves `Game` permanently un-disposed
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-020 — A throwing component leaves `Game` permanently un-disposed
**Severity: low · Confidence: VERIFIED · Area: `modules/runtime`**

`isDisposed_ = true` is set last, after all cleanup (`Game.cpp:651`). An exception from any
component's `Dispose()`, from the content manager, or from the graphics service aborts the
remaining cleanup and leaves the object not marked disposed — so a later `Dispose()` re-runs the
partially-completed teardown.
candidates.bible_target_evidence: component exceptions still escape before `isDisposed_` becomes true

candidates.title: Renderer-tracked resources are registered by raw address, and copies escape tracking
candidates.bible_body:
### CNA-BUG-029 — Renderer-tracked resources are registered by raw address, and copies escape tracking
**Severity: medium · Confidence: VERIFIED · Area: `modules/graphics`**

`GraphicsDevice` keeps a non-owning `std::vector<GraphicsResource*>`; registration happens in
`GraphicsResource`'s normal constructor, but the **copy constructor sets `graphicsDevice_` without
calling `AddResourceReference`** (`GraphicsResource.cpp:10-15` vs `:17-24`). A copied resource is
therefore untracked, is not disposed by `GraphicsDevice::Dispose()`, and — because `Texture2D` is
freely copyable by design (`Texture2D.hpp:96-100`) — can outlive its device and destroy a native
backend after the context is gone. Move construction transfers the handle while leaving the
moved-from address in the tracker.

This was recorded in the previous edition's audit as a `needs_human` item and is repeated here so
it is not lost: the policy choice (repair registration, or prohibit copy/move on tracked resources
with a deliberate `Texture2D` alias rule) is the project owner's, not the book's.

---
candidates.bible_target_evidence: current recovery registries still retain raw resource addresses; copy/move proof is incomplete

candidates.summary: Game::PollEvents calls the renderer's DebugSimulateContextLoss()/DebugRestoreContext() on any non-repeating F9/F10 key press with no build-type or option guard; renderers that override the hooks (Direct2D, DirectX 9/11/12, EasyGL, WebGPU) will simulate a loss in a shipped game.
candidates.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (Game::PollEvents, KeyEvent branch); IGraphicsRenderer.hpp default no-ops
candidates.note: read from source; not confirmed whether the unguarded behavior is intended; recorded for the later bug catalogue, published on the page only as a factual note

candidates.summary: A documentation comment in the C API header content_readers.h refers to cna_get_last_error_message, which is not declared anywhere; the declared accessors are cna_error_get_last_info, cna_error_get_last_message_size and cna_error_copy_last_message
candidates.note: documentation drift in CNA; the page names the declared accessors

candidates.note: stated on the page with attribution and as a baseline only

candidates.summary: Reordering Game's data members is not guarded by any assertion; the platform-outlives-dependents rule is held by declaration order and comments only
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: The header comment of GraphicsRendererSelection says the latch closes when the first device begins construction; the code latches at the end of a successful resolveRenderer
candidates.note: documentation lag in CNA; the page states the code behaviour

candidates.summary: A newly added GraphicsCapability enumerator is answered true by the default IGraphicsRenderer::SupportsCapability unless the device routes it to an opt-in query; nothing enforces an explicit answer per renderer
candidates.note: documented by comments in the source; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: With IsFixedTimeStep true and TargetElapsedTime greater than MaxElapsedTime (500 ms) the accumulator is clamped below one step every tick, so Update never runs while Draw does.
candidates.evidence: modules/runtime/src/Game.cpp (Tick: clamp to MaxElapsedTime before while accumulated >= TargetElapsedTime)
candidates.note: source-read edge case, no test; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: The Emscripten frame body ignores IsFixedTimeStep=false, suppressDraw_ and isSuspended_, advances TotalGameTime before Update, gives the first update a full step, always reports IsRunningSlowly false, and swallows a frame exception (logs it, then Run() returns normally without OnExiting).
candidates.note: documented for authors in docs/game-loop.html; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: F9 and F10 are consumed by every Game (renderer DebugSimulateContextLoss / DebugRestoreContext) with no opt-out.
candidates.note: debug hook by design; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: If the platform performance counter never advances, the fixed-step wait loops spin forever; nothing guards it.
candidates.note: contract-guarded by GamePlatformTimingTests, not defended in code

candidates.summary: Game::InactiveSleepTime is stored, validated and returned by the C API getter/setter but nothing in the loop reads it: the desktop Tick does not sleep while IsActive is false.
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue

candidates.summary: CNA::Runtime and CNA::RuntimeOptions are declared in CNA/Misc.hpp but never defined; a call would fail to link. A CMake check keeps the C API coverage record honest.
candidates.note: known and guarded; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: GameComponentCollection's own items_/owned_ have no lock; concurrent mutation, or mutation during Game::Initialize/Dispose(true)/DoInitialize iteration, is unprotected. A component added from LoadContent is categorized but its Initialize() is not called by the base path.
candidates.note: limit of the documented threading rule; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: GraphicsDeviceManager lifetime is only safe when nested inside its game: its ClientSizeChanged subscription is never removed, Game caches raw manager/service pointers that unregisterServices does not clear, and ~GraphicsDeviceManager dereferences its Game. No test covers the unsupported shapes.
candidates.note: source-read constraint, not an observed crash; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: Game::IsMouseVisible forwards to IPlatformMouse::SetCursorVisible whenever a window and a mouse service exist; TerminalMouse::SetCursorVisible always throws PlatformException (same item as the Terminal ledger).
candidates.note: cross-reference; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: UnloadContent is reached only through explicit disposal with a registered graphics device service, after Content_.Dispose(); it never runs from ~Game or Run() returning.
candidates.note: XNA-parity-shaped limit, undocumented on the user side; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: After the last game uninstalls its platform, any static API that calls GetCurrentPlatform() during member teardown would lazily create a new default platform (immortal holder) instead of failing.
candidates.note: source-read hazard; HasCurrentPlatform is the non-creating probe; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: Manager-lifetime shapes not protected: manager destroyed while the game runs, or manager outliving an undisposed game (see module ledger).
candidates.note: duplicate of the module-ledger item

candidates.summary: Shared-owned components are destroyed after the device, content manager, window and services; a component destructor that calls back through its Game reference would touch destroyed members.
candidates.note: consequence of member order; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: A game without a GraphicsDeviceManager never gets UnloadContent from disposal (Game::Initialize subscribes only to a registered IGraphicsDeviceService); demo_2d is such a game.
candidates.note: documented XNA-parity limit; recorded for the later bug catalogue

candidates.summary: A comment in StorageDeviceTests.cpp still describes the storage root as an SDL pref-path directory; StorageDevice no longer uses SDL (root from XDG_DATA_HOME, LOCALAPPDATA, HOME, then the working directory).
candidates.note: Stale comment only; recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published.

candidates.summary: Game's frame snapshot nulling is not ordered against a removal performed on another thread while the game thread iterates; GameComponentCollection itself has no lock, so concurrent Add (loader) and Remove (game thread) race on items_.
candidates.note: Source reading only; no test exercises it and XNA does not promise it either. Recorded for the later bug catalogue as a scope limit, not a confirmed defect.

candidates.summary: StorageDeviceDeleteContainerTest recursively deletes a fixed per-user directory resolved from the real environment (XDG_DATA_HOME/LOCALAPPDATA/HOME) and its TearDown creates <data root>/game as a side effect.
candidates.note: Test-hygiene hazard, recorded for the later bug catalogue; not a product defect.

candidates.summary: StorageDevice's process-static root (storageRoot_, appName_, storageRootInitialized_) is unsynchronized; concurrent SetAppNameEXT and storage access is not covered.
candidates.note: Scope limit from source reading; no test.

candidates.summary: ContentManager::Unload() only clears loadedAssets_; disposables are recorded only through an explicit callback (ContentReader::RecordDisposable's manager fallback is marked deferred), while ContentManager::ReadAsset's doc comment says 'when empty, this manager records them itself, as Load<T>() does'.
candidates.note: Doc/code mismatch plus an XNA divergence (XNA's Unload disposes recorded assets); recorded for the later bug catalogue.

candidates.summary: cna_game_destroy's comment says Shutdown has already disposed the canonical graphics device, but Game::Dispose(true) disposes only the registered IGraphicsDeviceService, which does not dispose a Game-owned device.
candidates.note: Unconfirmed: source reading only, C API not built or run; may affect whether C subscribers observe the device's Disposing event. Not published on the page.

candidates.summary: DevicesShutdownCoordinator::Shutdown() must be called by the application before platform shutdown when VibrateController may have been used; neither Game nor the runtime calls it.
candidates.note: Documented contract, not a defect; an atexit fallback exists.

candidates.summary: The X11Platform class comment says every Xlib call goes through one per-instance mutex; no such mutex exists in modules/platform/src/X11 (only the process-wide error-policy mutex).
candidates.note: Documentation/code mismatch; the page states the sentence is not backed by readable code. Recorded for the later bug catalogue.

candidates.summary: Renderer context leases (EasyGL, OpenGL4) keep nesting state in a thread_local map; a release on a thread other than the acquiring one logs an error and returns without unlocking the recursive mutex.
candidates.note: Potential hazard if a lease object is ever moved across threads; not observed. Source reading only.

candidates.summary: GameComponentCollection storage and Game::Exit are unsynchronized while Game guards its derived component lists for loading-thread adds.
candidates.note: Scoped gap, documented on the page as what the guard does not cover; not a defect claim.

candidates.summary: XNB ContentTypeReaderManager registries and the ContentManager asset cache have no lock while the CNB loader registry uses a shared_mutex.
candidates.note: Asymmetry; matters only if readers are registered while a loader thread loads.

candidates.summary: docs/c-api/LIMITATIONS.md still says 'Four of the 49 renderers'; the snapshot has 25 renderer identities.
candidates.note: Stale CNA document noticed while reading; unrelated to threading; not repeated on the page.

candidates.summary: No production code calls Microsoft::Devices::Detail::DevicesShutdownCoordinator::Shutdown(); applications rely on the atexit fallback and PlatformVibrateBackend::ReleaseService's current-platform guard; the ordering harness covers SDL3/POSIX only
candidates.note: recorded for the later bug catalogue; not published as a catalogue; a consequence, not a proven defect

candidates.summary: FileDialog::ShowOpenFile/ShowSaveFile/ShowOpenFolder swallow PlatformException after moving the callback, so a rejected request produces no callback at all (unlike the no-service path, which reports an empty result).
candidates.note: Documented in a source comment as accepted; recorded for the later bug catalogue.

candidates.summary: StorageDeviceDeleteContainerTest teardown calls remove_all on a storage root derived from the caller's environment (XDG_DATA_HOME, LOCALAPPDATA, HOME, working directory).
candidates.note: A test-safety hazard rather than a product defect; the page instructs redirecting the environment root.

candidates.note: Consequence for a CNA_ENABLE_SDL=OFF configuration selecting STUB with tests on was not verified; recorded for the later bug catalogue.
